title: AEGIS structured log record, version 1
description: One JSON Lines record (AEGIS-232). Logs are machine-readable first: a run that cannot be joined back to its experiment, or ordered deterministically, is not evidence of anything.

schema_version.description: Version of this record shape. Present on every record so a reader can reject what it does not understand instead of misparsing it.

timestamp_ns.description: UTC nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, taken from an injected clock. Never a monotonic reading: those are meaningful only within one process run and would replay to different values.

logger.description: Component that emitted the record, e.g. 'exchange.sequencer'.

experiment_id.description: The run this record belongs to. The same field appears in the message envelope, so a log line and an event can be joined without a lookup table (AEGIS-209, AEGIS-232).

correlation_id.description: Identifier tying a record to one causal chain — an order, a decision, a replayed event.

sequence.description: Monotone per logger instance. Two records sharing a timestamp still have a defined order, which is what makes a log file hashable for determinism checks (AEGIS-005).

fields.description: Structured payload. Scalars only: a nested blob defeats the point of machine-readable logs and invites unbounded records on a hot path.
